memory: Another significant benefit of research is the opportunity to connect with professors on a more personal level. My principal investigator(PI) is incredibly approachable, and I can easily pop into her office to discuss anything from career direction to academic struggles. She's been instrumental in recommending me for various scholarships, events, and networking opportunities. I recently had the chance to attend a virtual workshop on immersive analytics, which brought together academic experts from around the world. Witnessing them debate technical details, propose new frameworks, and engage in light-hearted banter over rival theories was truly fascinating. It felt like I was experiencing the cutting-edge of CS knowledge in real time.That's a summary of my journey in the research world so far. It's been a lot of hard work, often more chaotic than expected, but also incredibly rewarding. I love the feeling that what I do in the lab might contribute to scientists understanding their data in a new way five or ten years down the line. Maybe one day the VR and immersive technologies we're pioneering will become standard tools, and I'll be able to look back and say, 'I was part of that from the beginning.' It's the sense of contributing to something bigger that keeps me motivated. Whether or not I decide to pursue a graduate degree soon, this experience has changed how I think about computer science, innovation, and teamwork. I couldn't imagine my undergraduate years without it—it's definitely enriched my perspective on what it means to be a computer scientist.
